scopeAuthority.rule: Core questions map to TP 15263 Section 5 maps and charts, with NAV CANADA and TC AIM support. The Coastal Drone article is secondary instructional context only.

questions.question: On a Canadian VNC or VTA, how is Class F Special Use Airspace commonly identified in the chart legend and on the chart?
choices: By a defined boundary with inward-facing perpendicular marks and an identifier such as CYA, CYR, or CYD
Only by a solid green circle with no identifier
Only by a runway symbol and aerodrome elevation
By a blue airway centreline with no area code
questions.rationale: Canadian Class F Advisory, Restricted, and Danger areas are depicted with a defined boundary, inward-facing perpendicular marks, and a CYA, CYR, or CYD identifier. The current DAH supplies the controlling boundaries, altitudes, activity, and status information.
questions.knowledgeTopic: VNC/VTA legend - Class F Special Use Airspace
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the chart notation and identifier used for Canadian Class F Special Use Airspace and cross-reference the area in the DAH.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 5 - Maps and charts; NAV CANADA VNC/VTA legend; Designated Airspace Handbook; Coastal Drone VNC legend article

questions.question: In a Canadian Class F chart label such as CYA 118(A)(T)(H), what do the letters in parentheses indicate?
choices: The activity types associated with the area, such as aerobatic, training, and hang-gliding activity
The controlling agency, chart edition, and magnetic variation
The airspace class, floor, and ceiling in hundreds of feet
The aerodrome category, runway surface, and lighting status
questions.rationale: The parenthetical activity codes identify the type of activity associated with the Class F area. The DAH remains the authoritative source for the area's current dimensions, altitudes, times, and controlling or using agency.
questions.knowledgeTopic: VNC/VTA legend - Class F activity codes
questions.learningObjective: Interpret common Class F activity codes shown with a CYA, CYR, or CYD chart identifier.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 5 - Maps and charts; NAV CANADA VNC/VTA legend; Designated Airspace Handbook; Coastal Drone VNC legend article

questions.question: On an air/ground communication box in the Canadian VNC legend, what does a heavy box line generally indicate?
choices: The standard FSS frequencies are available at the station shown
The frequencies are available only from a remote site shown below the box
The area is Class F Restricted airspace
The box is an aerodrome elevation and runway-data box
questions.rationale: The Canadian VNC legend uses the heavy communication-box line to identify an FSS with standard group frequencies available at that station. Communication information should still be checked against current publications before flight.
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the meaning of line weight in a Canadian VNC air/ground communication box.
questions.source: TP 15263 Section 5 - Maps and charts; NAV CANADA VNC/VTA legend; Coastal Drone VNC legend article

questions.question: An ICAO aerodrome entry shows a local magnetic variation such as W 11°. What does that value help a pilot determine?
choices: The relationship between true directions on the chart and magnetic headings used for navigation
The maximum legal takeoff weight of an aircraft at the nearest aerodrome
Whether a Class F area is active today without checking the DAH or NOTAMs
The radio frequency used by every aircraft in the charted area
questions.rationale: The magnetic variation published with an aerodrome indicates the local difference between true and magnetic direction. It helps relate true directions used on charts to magnetic headings used by compass-based navigation; it does not replace current airspace status, NOTAM, or aerodrome information.
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the magnetic variation published with an ICAO aerodrome and relate true directions to magnetic headings.
